deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page (95r) Riemann takes a large set of integer summation variables m^{α,β}_ν, with α a primitive λ-th root of unity, g a primitive root mod λ, κ = 1..2μ and 2μ = λ−1. He forms their finite Fourier transforms n^{α,κ}_ν = Σ_β m^{α,(−1)^κβ}_ν α^{βg^κ}, i.e. the 2μ conjugate embeddings of cyclotomic integers. He rewrites a big quadratic form (coefficients r, s, a, b, c) in these variables. Since g^μ ≡ −1 (mod λ), α^{g^{κ+μ}} is the complex conjugate of α^{g^κ}. So n^{κ+μ} = conj(n^κ), and indices κ and κ+μ pair up as conjugate eigenspaces. This page draws the theta-function consequences.

Line 1. The original theta series is rewritten in the transformed variables:
Σ exp( (2/λ) Σ_κ^{(ρ−1)} Σ_{ν,ν'}^{2μ} b^κ_{νν'} n^{κ+μ}_ν n^κ_{ν'} + (2/λ) Σ v^κ_ν n^κ_ν + (1/λ) Σ_{ν,ν'}^{ρ} a_{νν'} n_ν n_{ν'} + (2/λ) Σ_ν u_ν n_ν ).
The summation is subject to the congruence conditions written at the right: n^κ_ν ≡ n_ν (mod ρ) and n_ρ ≡ 0 (mod ρ). So the series splits into a rational part, with the a-form and u-variables, and a cyclotomic part. In the cyclotomic part the form b^κ n^{κ+μ} n^κ is Hermitian, since n^{κ+μ} = conj(n^κ). It is definite once Re b < 0; for genuinely independent integers n^κ, n^{κ+μ} the form n·n' would be indefinite. That is why the n^κ must be read as conjugates.

Line 2. Riemann drops the congruences ("n^κ_ν alle ganzen Zahlen") and isolates the theta function
ϑ(v) = Σ exp( (2/λ) Σ b^κ_{νν'} n^{κ+μ}_ν n^κ_{ν'} + (2/λ) Σ v^κ_ν n^κ_ν ).
He then lists its properties:
(i) ϑ(v^κ_ν) = ϑ(α^{g^κ} v^κ_ν). Multiplying n by the unit α permutes the lattice, so the root of unity acts as an automorphism (complex multiplication by Z[α]).
(ii) ϑ(v^κ + g_κ πi) = ϑ. The periods are πi times the conjugates g_κ of a cyclotomic integer.
(iii) A quasi-periodicity of the form log ϑ(v + b_{ν,·}) = log ϑ(v) + (2/λ)·(linear in v) + (2/λ)·(constant in b).

Line 3. He replaces the argument by ρ^{κ+κ'} v^κ, where ρ^{κ+κ'} denotes the conjugates of a cyclotomic integer ρ (cf. 96r, τ_κ = α^{g^κ} − α^{−g^κ}, written τ_{κ+κ'}). So ϑ(ρ^{κ+κ'} v) is the pull-back of ϑ under a complex-multiplication endomorphism. Translating the summation by n → n + ρ^{κ+κ'}, he records the transformed quasi-periodicity. In it the linear term acquires factors ρ^{κ+κ'} ρ^{κ+κ'+μ}, i.e. |ρ^{(κ)}|².

Lines 4–5 (Riemann's zero-sum argument, transposed). On the Riemann surface the function ϑ(ρ^{κ+κ'}(v^κ − e^κ)) has a fixed number of zeros, written "Σ(ρ^κ−1)λ mal σ" with τ = 1 … 2(ρ−1)λ (reading uncertain). The counting factor should be related to the norm of ρ. The zeros have Abel integrals ∫ dv^κ_ν = β^{κ,τ}_ν.
He integrates log ϑ(ρ^{κ+κ'}(v − e)) dv^κ_{ν'} around the boundary of the dissected surface. The jumps of log ϑ across the cuts come from the quasi-periodicity of line 3. The result is
2πi Σ_τ β^{κ,τ}_{ν'} = Σ_{ν''} Σ_g ∫ (2/λ)(…) e^κ_{ν''} α^{−ρg} ρρ̄ dv^κ_{ν'} α^{ρg} + const = 2πi e^{κ''}_{ν'} ρ^{κ''+κ'} ρ^{κ''+κ'+μ} + const.
That is, the sum of the Abel images of the zeros equals e multiplied by ρ·ρ̄ (the norm-type factor), up to Riemann's constants. This is the analogue of Riemann's theorem Σ β = e + k for the pulled-back theta function.

Line 6. He abbreviates f^κ_ν = e^κ_ν ρ^{κ+κ'}.

Line 7. He writes a candidate function of two points (u, v) and (u', v'):
Σ Ω(u − u', v − v' − f) · Ω(u − u', v − v' + α^{g^{κ+κ'}} f) / [ ϑ(ρ^{κ+κ'} v − f) · ϑ(ρ^{κ+κ'} v' + f) ].
Here Ω is presumably the theta function of the full (rational × cyclotomic) problem. This is the standard Riemann device: a quotient of theta products in the difference of two points, normalised by the zero-producing denominators, designed to be single-valued. It is used to express a third-kind integral or the transformation via ϑ(ρv).

Lines 8–10. These are scratch checks of the shifted arguments needed to verify the quasi-periodicity factors of the quotient. They compare Σβ − v ρρ̄ and the arguments ρ^{κ+κ'+μ} v ± f α^{κ+κ'+μ}. They are fragmentary.

Overall, the page treats the theta function of an abelian variety with complex multiplication by the cyclotomic field Q(α). It shows how the original theta decomposes under a congruence mod ρ, and studies the composition with multiplication by ρ via Riemann's zero-sum theorem. This is a step toward a transformation (multiplication) formula. The next page (96r) carries out the corresponding theta inversion and continued-fraction reduction in the variables τ_κ.
errors:
Quasi-periodicity sign/index (my check): with exponent (2/λ)(b n_κ n_{κ+μ} + v_κ n_κ + v_{κ+μ} n_{κ+μ}), shifting v_κ by b and re-indexing n_{κ+μ} → n_{κ+μ} − 1 gives log ϑ(v_κ + b) = log ϑ(v) − (2/λ) v_{κ+μ}.
  - The linear term should carry a minus sign and the conjugate index κ+μ.
  - There is no b-constant unless the coefficient of n^{κ+μ}n^κ is doubled, as happens when b^κ and b^{κ+μ} both contribute.
  - Riemann writes '+ (2/λ)Σ v^κ_{ν'} + (2/λ)Σ b'. This is either a convention difference or a slip; it cannot be decided from the fragment.
In line 2 the b-term lost its variables n^{κ+μ}_ν n^κ_{ν'}, and the upper limit is written μ instead of 2μ. This is a copying slip.
'n^κ_ν alle ganzen Zahlen' must mean all cyclotomic-integer tuples (n^{κ+μ} = conj n^κ). For literally independent integers the form b n n' is indefinite and the series diverges.
The zero count 'Σ(ρ^κ−1)λ mal σ', τ = 1…2(ρ−1)λ, is not clearly justified on the page. The expected count for ϑ∘ρ should involve the norm N(ρ) times the genus-type count; the relation is unverified.
The final equality in the zero-sum line drops the sums over g and ν'' and the constant without comment. This is plausibly intended, but it is an unjustified step as written.

results.what: Decomposition of a theta series into a rational part and a cyclotomic part after a discrete Fourier transform over a cyclic group, with congruence conditions mod ρ
results.modern_name: Theta functions of abelian varieties with an automorphism / complex multiplication by Z[ζ_λ]; isotypic decomposition of the period lattice
results.usually_credited_to: Theory of CM abelian varieties: Shimura–Taniyama (1950s–61). Theta of curves with automorphisms: Wirtinger, Schottky (late 19th c.)

results.what: Invariance ϑ(α^{g^κ} v^κ) = ϑ(v) and periods g_κ πi given by conjugates of cyclotomic integers
results.modern_name: Complex multiplication by roots of unity acting on the Jacobian of a cyclic cover (e.g. y^λ = …)
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in work on cyclic curves (Wirtinger 1895, later Shimura)

results.what: Riemann zero-sum argument (contour integral of log ϑ dv) applied to the pulled-back function ϑ(ρ(v − e)), giving Σβ = ρρ̄·e + const
results.modern_name: Riemann's vanishing/zero theorem applied to an isogeny (multiplication by a CM endomorphism)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1857) for the basic theorem; the CM-endomorphism version is folklore and later

results.what: Quotient of products of theta functions in point differences used to build single-valued functions or third-kind integrals
results.modern_name: Theta-quotient (prime-form-type) construction of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann is known to have studied theta functions and transformation theory, and Nachlass work on cyclic/cyclotomic period structures is mentioned in the literature. Still, a systematic treatment of the theta function of a Jacobian with complex multiplication by Z[ζ_λ], including pull-back by a cyclotomic endomorphism ρ, would be a notable unpublished detail. The page is fragmentary and the interpretation partly conjectural, so the score is moderate rather than high.

checkable.sympy: lam=7; g=3; mu=3; all(pow(g,k+mu,lam)==(-pow(g,k,lam))%lam for k in range(1,2*mu+1))
checkable.asserts: For λ = 7 and primitive root g = 3, g^{κ+μ} ≡ −g^κ (mod λ). Hence α^{g^{κ+μ}} = conj(α^{g^κ}), which underlies the pairing κ ↔ κ+μ.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; a=exp(2*pi*I/7); m=[1,2,0,-1,3,1]; nk=lambda k: sum(m[b]*a**((b+1)*pow(3,k,7)) for b in range(6)); simplify(nk(1+3)-conjugate(nk(1)))
checkable.asserts: n^{κ+μ} is the complex conjugate of n^κ. The output should simplify to 0 (numerically ~0).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; b=Symbol('b'); v=Symbol('v'); w=Symbol('w'); lam=Integer(7); T=lambda v,w,N=6: sum(exp((2/lam)*(b*m*n+v*m+w*n)) for m in range(-N,N+1) for n in range(-N,N+1)); # compare T(v+b,w) with exp(-(2/lam)*w)*T(v,w) termwise via reindexing n->n-1
checkable.asserts: Model quasi-periodicity check: exponent shift identity (2/λ)(b m n + (v+b) m + w n) = (2/λ)(b m (n+1) + v m + w (n+1)) − (2/λ) w. Hence ϑ(v+b) = e^{−2w/λ} ϑ(v) once the summation is re-indexed. Convergence in the genuine case needs the conjugate (Hermitian) structure; this is a formal check of the exponent only.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; b,v,w,m,n=symbols('b v w m n'); lam=Symbol('lam'); simplify((2/lam)*(b*m*n+(v+b)*m+w*n) - ((2/lam)*(b*m*(n+1)+v*m+w*(n+1)) - (2/lam)*w))
checkable.asserts: Exact algebraic identity behind the quasi-periodicity (equals 0).

transcription_corrections: Line 2: the b-term should carry n^{κ+μ}_ν n^κ_{ν'} as in line 1. The transcription drops the variables, but they are omitted in the manuscript too.
'ϑ(v^κ_ν) = ϑ(α^κ v^κ_ν)' should read ϑ(α^{g^κ} v^κ_ν): the exponent of α is g^κ.
The first-line prefix is a struck-out symbol before e, not a summation; the struck-out item before 'Σ(ρ^κ−1)λ' is a deleted 'ϑ(ρ^{κ+κ'} …)'.
In the Ω-quotient the second Ω argument reads v^κ_ν − v'^κ_ν + α^{g^{κ+κ'}} f^κ_ν (α raised to g^{κ+κ'}).
In the scratch lines 'ρ^{κ+κ'+μ}_{κ+κ'}' is two separate factors ρ^{κ+κ'} ρ^{κ+κ'+μ} (written ρ ρ with superscripts), not a subscripted symbol.
